ei.title: Chapter 5-13 Analysis: Speech: Communication, Not Performance
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are (A)[concerned / indifferent] about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute (B)[imperfection / perfection] in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more (C)[human / robotic].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 사람들은 실수를 걱정하고(concerned), 절대적 완벽함(perfection)의 잣대로 평가받는다고 느끼며, 실수가 화자를 더 인간적으로(human) 보이게 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① indifferent — perfection — human (A 반대: 걱정하는→무관심한)
❌ ② concerned — imperfection — human (B 반대: 완벽함→불완전함)
❌ ③ concerned — perfection — robotic (C 반대: 인간적인→로봇 같은)
✅ ④ concerned — perfection — human — 원문 일치 ←정답

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or (A)[awkward / graceful] gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a (B)[amateur / virtuoso] performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas (C)[clearly / vaguely] and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 어색한(awkward) 몸짓이 불리하게 작용하고, 청중은 거장다운(virtuoso) 연주를 바라는 게 아니며, 화자의 생각을 명확하게(clearly) 전달하는 연설을 원한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① graceful — virtuoso — clearly (A 반대: 어색한→우아한)
❌ ② awkward — amateur — clearly (B 반대: 거장의→아마추어의)
✅ ③ awkward — virtuoso — clearly — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ awkward — virtuoso — vaguely (C 반대: 명확하게→모호하게)

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of (A)[absolute / partial] perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and (B)[indirectly / directly]. Sometimes an error or two can actually (C)[enhance / diminish] a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 청중은 절대적(absolute) 완벽함의 잣대로 평가하고, 좋은 연설은 생각을 직접적으로(directly) 전달하며, 한두 개의 실수가 화자의 매력을 높일(enhance) 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① partial — directly — enhance (A 반대: 절대적인→부분적인)
❌ ② absolute — indirectly — enhance (B 반대: 직접적으로→간접적으로)
❌ ③ absolute — directly — diminish (C 반대: 높이다→줄이다)
✅ ④ absolute — directly — enhance — 원문 일치 ←정답

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a ①<u>mistake</u> in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is ②<u>judging</u> them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that ③<u>conceals</u> the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more ④<u>human</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '숨기다(conceals)'가 아니라 '전달하다(communicates)'가 문맥상 적절하다. 좋은 연설은 화자의 생각을 명확하고 직접적으로 전달한다.
det.analysis:
① mistake — 실수, 원문 일치
② judging — 평가하는, 원문 일치
③ conceals — 원문은 communicates(전달하다) ←정답
④ human — 인간적인, 원문 일치

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are ①<u>concerned</u> about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute ②<u>perfection</u> in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a ③<u>virtuoso</u> performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more ④<u>mechanical</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '기계적인(mechanical)'이 아니라 '인간적인(human)'이 문맥상 적절하다. 실수는 오히려 화자를 더 인간적으로 보이게 하여 매력을 높인다.
det.analysis:
① concerned — 걱정하는, 원문 일치
② perfection — 완벽함, 원문 일치
③ virtuoso — 거장의, 원문 일치
④ mechanical — 원문은 human(인간적인) ←정답

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or ①<u>awkward</u> gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like ②<u>fans</u> in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out ③<u>address</u> that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's ④<u>appeal</u> by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: '팬(fans)'이 아니라 '심사위원(judges)'이 문맥상 적절하다. 연설 청중은 바이올린 연주회의 심사위원처럼 흠을 잡지 않는다는 대조이다.
det.analysis:
① awkward — 어색한, 원문 일치
② fans — 원문은 judges(심사위원) ←정답
③ address — 연설, 원문 일치
④ appeal — 매력, 원문 일치

❌ ③ freedom — 자유 (완벽함의 잣대와 무관)

det.tip: a scale of absolute perfection = 절대적 완벽함의 잣대

det.korean: 사람들은 연설을 의사소통(communication)의 행위가 아니라 공연으로 여긴다.
det.analysis:

❌ ③ repetition — 반복 (문맥과 무관)
❌ ④ imitation — 모방 (문맥과 무관)

det.korean: 잘못 말한 단어나 어색한 몸짓(gesture)이 화자에게 불리하게 작용한다.

✅ ③ gesture — 몸짓 ←정답
❌ ④ question — 질문 (몸짓이 아님)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 enhance의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: enhance = 향상시키다 → improve(개선하다, 높이다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① weaken — 약화시키다 (반의어)
✅ ② improve — 개선하다, 높이다 ←정답
❌ ③ delay — 지연시키다 (의미축 다름)
❌ ④ replace — 대체하다 (향상과 무관)

det.korean: appeal = 매력 → charm(매력, 매혹)
det.analysis:
✅ ① charm — 매력 ←정답
❌ ② threat — 위협 (매력과 반대 뉘앙스)
❌ ③ duty — 의무 (의미축 다름)

det.korean: concerned(걱정하는) ↔ indifferent(무관심한)
det.analysis:
❌ ① worried — 걱정하는 (동의어)
❌ ② nervous — 초조한 (동의어 뉘앙스)
✅ ③ indifferent — 무관심한 ←정답

det.korean: clearly(명확하게) ↔ vaguely(모호하게)
det.analysis:
❌ ① plainly — 분명하게 (동의어)
✅ ② vaguely — 모호하게 ←정답
❌ ③ honestly — 정직하게 (의미축 다름)

questions.passage:
(A) The mayor delivered an inspiring <u>address</u> at the graduation ceremony.

(B) Please write your home <u>address</u> clearly on the envelope.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 address의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 시장이 졸업식에서 감동적인 연설(speech)을 했다 / (B) 봉투에 집 주소(location)를 명확히 쓰세요
det.analysis:
✅ ① 연설 — 주소 ←정답
❌ ② 주소 — 연설 (A는 '연설', B는 '주소'로 순서가 반대)
❌ ③ 연설 — 연설 (B는 '주소'이지 '연설'이 아님)
❌ ④ 주소 — 주소 (A는 '연설'이지 '주소'가 아님)
det.tip: address: (A) 연설(a formal speech) vs (B) 주소(a location)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a person who is extremely skilled at something, especially at playing a musical instrument"

det.korean: 어떤 것, 특히 악기 연주에 매우 능숙한 사람 → virtuoso(거장, 명연주자)

✅ ① virtuoso — 거장, 명연주자 ←정답
❌ ② amateur — 아마추어 (숙련되지 않은 사람, 반대)
❌ ③ beginner — 초보자 (매우 능숙함과 반대)
❌ ④ critic — 비평가 (연주자가 아닌 평가자)
det.tip: virtuoso = 거장, 명연주자 (an extremely skilled performer)

questions.passage: They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that __________ (communicate) the speaker's ideas clearly and directly.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 화자의 생각을 명확하고 직접적으로 전달하는(communicates) 연설 → 선행사 address(단수)를 받는 관계대명사 that 뒤의 동사는 단수형
det.analysis: address that __________ (communicate) the speaker's ideas → 선행사가 단수 address이고 that이 주격 관계대명사이므로 3인칭 단수 동사 → communicates. communicate(전달하다, 원형)를 communicates(단수형)로 변환.
det.tip: communicate(원형) → communicates (단수 선행사 address를 받는 주격 관계대명사 동사)

questions.passage: They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every __________ (misstate) word or awkward gesture will count against them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 잘못 말한(misstated) 단어 → 명사 word를 앞에서 수식하는 과거분사 형태
det.analysis: every __________ (misstate) word → 명사 word를 수식하는 자리이고 '잘못 말해진' 수동의 의미이므로 과거분사 → misstated. misstate(잘못 말하다, 원형)를 misstated(과거분사, 형용사적 수식)로 변환.
det.tip: misstate(잘못 말하다, 원형) → misstated (명사 word를 수식하는 과거분사)
